statement.p:
We will look at some examples of bases in this activity.
In the preview activity, we worked with the set of vectors in \real^2:
\vvec_1 = \twovec{2}{1}, \vvec_2 = \twovec{1}{2} . Explain why these vectors form a basis for \real^2.
Consider the set of vectors in \real^3
\vvec_1 = \threevec{1}{1}{1}, \vvec_2 = \threevec{0}{1}{-1}, \vvec_3 = \threevec{1}{0}{-1}
and determine whether they form a basis for \real^3.
Do the vectors
\vvec_1 = \threevec{-2}{1}{3}, \vvec_2 = \threevec{3}{0}{-1}, \vvec_3 = \threevec{1}{1}{0}, \vvec_4 = \threevec{0}{3}{-2}
form a basis for \real^3?
Explain why the vectors \evec_1,\evec_2,\evec_3 form a basis for \real^3.
If a set of vectors \vvec_1,\vvec_2,\ldots,\vvec_n forms a basis for \real^m, what can you guarantee about the pivot positions of the matrix
\left[\begin{array}{rrrr} \vvec_1 \amp \vvec_2 \amp \ldots \amp \vvec_n \end{array}\right] ?
If the set of vectors \vvec_1,\vvec_2,\ldots,\vvec_n is a basis for \real^{10}, how many vectors must be in the set?

li.p: The matrix \left[\begin{array}{rr} \vvec_1 \amp \vvec_2 \end{array}\right] is row equivalent to the identity matrix so it has a pivot position in every row. The span of the columns is therefore \real^2. There is also a pivot position in every column, which means that the columns are linearly independent.

The matrix whose columns are the vectors \vvec_1, \vvec_2, \vvec_3, and \vvec_4 has dimensions 3\times4. Therefore, there cannot be a pivot position in every column, which tells us that the columns cannot be linearly independent. Therefore, the set of vectors do not form a basis for \real^3.

Putting these vectors into a matrix produces the identity matrix, which has a pivot position in every row and every column. Therefore, the span of the vectors is \real^3, and they are linearly independent.
There must be a pivot position in every row and every column.

A basis for \real^{10} must have 10 vectors. Because the associated matrix must have a pivot position in every row and every column, there must be the same number of columns as there are rows. Since the vectors are 10-dimensional, there must be 10 vectors.
